verdict.reasoning: Patient reports “pain…in my tummy, like the lower part of my tummy” starting “about two days ago” and says “I’ve just been feeling, quite, hot and sweaty.”

Location: “like below my belly button” (suprapubic/lower abdomen). Quality: “a burning pain.” Course: “it is getting a bit worse now.” Radiation: “It hasn’t spread anywhere else.” Constancy: “It’s pretty constant, it’s like getting worse.”
Patient says “Yeah, I had a bit of constipation, but that’s better, now. That was like, since last week… my bowel movements are normal now.”
Frequency: “I did notice I was going to the, I was peeing more, regularly… I have been drinking lots of fluids.” Color: “I did notice that I was a little, the urine was a little pink, in colour.”
Patient: “Just a little nauseous, um, but no vomiting.”
Patient: “I’ve just been feeling, quite, hot and sweaty” and later “I felt a bit hot and sweaty, but I haven’t really measured it, so I can’t really say.”

Sexual activity: “Yes… I have had the same partner… we were last sexually active about four days ago.” Contraception: “I’m, on the Implanon… inserted about a year ago.” Menses: When asked if still having periods, patient says “Yes.”

Transcript gives surgical and medication history but not explicit lack of medical conditions. Patient: “I haven’t had any, surgical… I don’t have any surgical history… I’m not on any other medication.” No explicit statement of “no prior medical conditions,” so that part is added.
Patient: “I’m, on the Implanon. I had the Implanon inserted about a year ago.”
Doctor asks about family history; patient replies: “No, not that, not that I’m aware of, no.”
Living situation: “I live in a share house, and with two other, two other room-mates.” Work: “I am an accountant.”
Smoking: Doctor: “Do you smoke at all, Kim?” Patient: “No.” Alcohol: “socially I drink, but uh, I don’t think more, more than normal.”
Resp: “I don’t feel short of breath… I don’t have a cough.” Cardiac: To palpitations: “Not that it, no.” Neuro/vision: “Any headaches? Any problems with your vision?” Patient: “No.”

Summarizes transcript: lower abdominal/suprapubic burning pain “about two days ago… getting a bit worse… pretty constant… It hasn’t spread anywhere else;” “a little nauseous;” “feeling hot and sweaty;” “some pink urine;” “no burning or stinging pain when you pass urine.” Doctor’s assessment: “Could just be a urine infection… something related to your gut… pregnancy-related cause.”

Doctor: “So, is there any chance you could be pregnant?… it’s something for us to think about… maybe worth taking a pregnancy test later on, just to confirm that.” This indicates pregnancy needs to be ruled out despite Implanon use.

Doctor: “start the antibiotics today, something called Trimethoprim. You can take two tablets, uh, one tablet twice a day for three days.” and “if I send it straight to your pharmacy.” This supports trimethoprim 1 tab BID x 3 days, e-prescription, start today (the “two tablets” phrase is corrected by the explicit dosing “one tablet twice a day”).

Doctor: “You can try just regular painkillers, Paracetamol would be advisable. Make sure you drink plenty of fluids. You can try some cranberry juice as well, which can sometimes help with your urine symptoms.”

Doctor: “maybe worth taking a pregnancy test later on, just to confirm that.” and “I still want you to bear in mind, you know, have a pregnancy test done to make sure we’re not missing anything else here.”
